```{r model outputs, echo = TRUE}
### ALL MODEL FRAMEWORKS PRESENTED BELOW BUT ONLY CERTAIN MODELS USED IN FINAL RESULTS ###

library(pacman)

# now select the packages I want in my workspace
p_load("tidycensus","tidyverse","dplyr","sf","ggplot2", "terra", "tidyterra", "tibble", "lme4", "raster", "MuMIn", "auk", "here", "exactextractr", "modelsummary", "gtsummary", "MASS", "sjPlot", "blackmarbler", "data.table", "tigris", "glmmTMB", "flextable")

# load in the needed datasets for the models so the knit works
urban_scaled <- st_read("~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2_ebird_eastbay/data/urban_scaled.gpkg")

tmp_data <- st_read("~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2_ebird_eastbay/data/covariate_tmp_data.gpkg")

 ## The luxury effect and bird biodiversity patterns ##
 # Response: Number of resident bird species
 # Predictors: Median income, housing density, rain, ALAN, and traffic volume
 # Model examples below, primary model is the glm.nb:
# now make the same model using the negative binomial
# testing resident bird diversity with 2020-2025 dataset
resident_model_area_offset <- glmmTMB(cbg_resident_richness ~ traffic_volume + ALAN + medincome + precip + offset(log_areakm2), 
data = urban_scaled, family = nbinom2) # nbinom2 is Negative Binomial
summary(resident_model_area_offset) # main model uses area_km2 as the offset, AIC = 10409.0
tab_model(resident_model_area_offset)
sjPlot::plot_model(resident_model_area_offset, type = "pred", colors = "blue3")

resident_model_chklst_ofst <- glmmTMB(cbg_resident_richness ~ traffic_volume + ALAN + medincome + precip + offset(log_checklist_km2), data = urban_scaled, family = nbinom2)
summary(resident_model_chklst_ofst) # AIC = 10975.8
# this model only uses offset log checklist density km2

resident_model_tmp_tract_re <- glmmTMB(cbg_resident_richness ~ traffic_volume + ALAN + medincome + precip + offset(log_checklist_km2) + (1 | tract_code), data = tmp_data, family = nbinom2)
summary(resident_model_tmp_tract_re)
AIC(resident_model_tmp_tract_re)
tab_model(resident_model_tmp_tract_re)

resident_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN <- glmmTMB(cbg_resident_richness ~ traffic_volume + (ndvi * ALAN) +  medincome + precip + offset(log_checklist_km2) + (1 | tract_code), data = tmp_data, family = nbinom2)
summary(resident_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN) # this is our best model
AIC(resident_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN)
tab_model(resident_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN)

# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- #
 # looking at migratory species in response to urban/enviro variable
 # how are migratory species responding to urban environments?
 # --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- #
 # migratory birds in response to urban environments and their composition
# Response variable: number of migratory species observed
# Predictor variables: Standard as above ^^^
# make model for the negative binomial version of this response variable
migratory_model_area_ofst <- glmmTMB(cbg_migrant_richness ~ traffic_volume + ALAN + medincome + precip + offset(log_areakm2), data = urban_scaled, family = nbinom2)
summary(migratory_model_area_ofst) # AIC = 12089.2
tab_model(migratory_model_area_ofst)
sjPlot::plot_model(migratory_model_area_ofst, type = "pred", colors = "red4")

migratory_model_chklst_ofst <- glmmTMB(cbg_migrant_richness ~ traffic_volume + ALAN + medincome + precip + offset(log_checklist_km2), data = urban_scaled, family = nbinom2)
summary(migratory_model_chklst_ofst) # AIC = 12811.7
tab_model(migratory_model_chklst_ofst)

migratory_model_tmp_tract_re <- glmmTMB(cbg_migrant_richness ~ traffic_volume + ALAN + medincome + precip + offset(log_checklist_km2) + (1 | tract_code), data = tmp_data, family = nbinom2)
summary(migratory_model_tmp_tract_re) # AIC = 12378.0
tab_model(migratory_model_tmp_tract_re)

migratory_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN <- glmmTMB(cbg_migrant_richness ~ traffic_volume + (ndvi * ALAN) +  medincome + precip + offset(log_checklist_km2) + (1 | tract_code), data = tmp_data, family = nbinom2)
summary(migratory_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN) # AIC = 12136.7

### Making Table for Ecological Model Outputs ###
# create list for the ecological models and grab the summary stats of interest

eco_models <- list(resident_model_area_offset, resident_model_chklst_ofst, "resident_model_chklst_tract_re" = resident_model_tmp_tract_re, "resident_model_chklst_trat_re_ndvi_alan" = resident_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN, migratory_model_area_ofst, migratory_model_chklst_ofst, "migratory_model_chklst_tract_re" = migratory_model_tmp_tract_re, "migratory_model_chklst_tract_re_ndvi_alan" = migratory_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN) # grab all the models so we can pull the info we need

# first we list the models with their respective names
 eco_model_list <- list(
   "Migratory Model 1" = migratory_model_area_ofst,
   "Migratory Model 2" = migratory_model_chklst_ofst,
   "Migratory Model 3" = migratory_model_tmp_tract_re,
   "Migratory Model 4" = migratory_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN,
   "Resident Model 1" = resident_model_area_offset,
   "Resident Model 2" = resident_model_chklst_ofst,
   "Resident Model 3" = resident_model_tmp_tract_re,
   "Resident Model 4" = resident_model_tmp_tract_re_w_NDVI_w_ALAN)
 
# Export this directly to the csv format
# modelsummary(eco_model_list, output = "~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2_ebird_eastbay/R_tables/eco_model_table.csv")
 
 # now we try to create a succint table using model summary
 ecomodeltable <- modelsummary::modelsummary(eco_model_list,
                            fmt = 2,
                            estimate = "{estimate} [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                            statistic = c("s.e. = {std.error}",
                                          "z = {statistic}",
                                          "p = {p.value}"),
                            metrics = c("AIC","F","RMSE"),
                            coef_omit = "Intercept",
                            stars = FALSE,
                            output = "tinytable")
 # looks good! Now save this.
 
 # double check the table and make sure it looks fine
 print(ecomodeltable) # looks good to me
 
 # make sure the Latex installation is in the system

## Analyzing the luxury effect and survey checklist dynamic ##
# Response: The number of survey checklists performed
# Predictors: Standard as above ^^^
# Model:
# now the glm negative binomial

# Checklist model with the 2020 - 2025 urban dataset
checklist_model <- glmmTMB(n_checklists ~ housing_density + medincome + traffic_volume + temp + offset(log_areakm2), data = urban_scaled, family = nbinom2)
summary(checklist_model) # AIC = 13298.1
tab_model(checklist_model)
plot_model(checklist_model, type = "pred", colors = "forestgreen")

checklist_model2 <- glmmTMB(n_checklists ~ housing_density + medincome + traffic_volume + temp, data = urban_scaled, family = nbinom2)
summary(checklist_model2) # AIC = 13567.1
tab_model(checklist_model2)

checklist_model3 <- glmmTMB(n_checklists ~ housing_density + medincome + traffic_volume + temp + offset(log_areakm2) + (1 | tract_code), data = tmp_data, family = nbinom2)
summary(checklist_model3) # AIC = 12840.6
tab_model(checklist_model3)

checklist_model4 <- glmmTMB(n_checklists ~ housing_density + medincome + traffic_volume + temp +
(1 | tract_code), data = tmp_data, family = nbinom2)
summary(checklist_model4) # AIC = 13107.4
tab_model(checklist_model4)
  
 ## The luxury effect and migration biomass ##
 # Response: Mean Migration Density (Spring stopover data from 2016-2020)
 # Predictors: nightlights, noise pollution, rain, income, housing density
 # model:
# Spring migration model with updated 2020-2025 dataset
radar_stopover_model <- glm(spring_migration ~ medincome + traffic_volume + ALAN + precip + offset(log_areakm2), family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = urban_scaled)
summary(radar_stopover_model) # AIC = 20538
tab_model(radar_stopover_model)
sjPlot::plot_model(radar_stopover_model, type = "pred", colors = "orange")

radar_stopover_model2 <- glm(spring_migration ~ medincome + traffic_volume + ALAN + precip, family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = urban_scaled)
summary(radar_stopover_model2) # AIC = 16667
tab_model(radar_stopover_model2)
sjPlot::plot_model(radar_stopover_model2, type = "pred", colors = "orange")

radar_stopover_model3 <- glm(spring_migration ~ medincome + traffic_volume + (ALAN * ndvi) + precip, family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = urban_scaled)
summary(radar_stopover_model3) # AIC = 16199
tab_model(radar_stopover_model3)
sjPlot::plot_model(radar_stopover_model3, type = "pred", colors = "orange")

radar_stopover_model4 <- glm(spring_migration ~ medincome + traffic_volume + (ALAN * ndvi) + offset(log_areakm2), family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = urban_scaled)
summary(radar_stopover_model4) # AIC = 20105
tab_model(radar_stopover_model4)
sjPlot::plot_model(radar_stopover_model4, type = "pred", colors = "orange")

### Making a table for the methodological model outputs ###
method_model_list <- list(
   "Checklist Model 1" = checklist_model,
   "Checklist Model 2" = checklist_model2,
   "Checklist Model 3" = checklist_model3,
   "Checklist Model 4" = checklist_model4,
   "Radar Model 1" = radar_stopover_model,
   "Radar Model 2" = radar_stopover_model2,
   "Radar Model 3" = radar_stopover_model3,
   "Radar Model 4" = radar_stopover_model4)
 
# Export this directly to the csv format
# modelsummary(eco_model_list, output = "~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2_ebird_eastbay/R_tables/eco_model_table.csv")
 
 # now we try to create a succint table using model summary
 methodmodeltable <- modelsummary::modelsummary(method_model_list,
                            fmt = 2,
                            estimate = "{estimate} [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                            statistic = c("s.e. = {std.error}",
                                          "z = {statistic}",
                                          "p = {p.value}"),
                            metrics = c("AIC", "RMSE"),
                            coef_omit = "Intercept",
                            stars = FALSE,
                            output = "tinytable")
 # looks good! Now save this.
 
 # double check the table and make sure it looks fine
 methodmodeltable # looks good to me

```
